scope: A shared SDK/CRT-free buffer-only policy replaces four independent D3D8/9 VB/IB Lock rejection blocks. XP-compatible HRESULT acceptance follows Wine Windows observations; effective access/streaming hints follow separately frozen Wine map conversion/sanitization facts. Static/CPU-only streaming hints are ignored, simultaneous DISCARD/NOOVERWRITE uses NOOVERWRITE, contradictory read-only hints use safe writable fallback, and genuine read-only maps skip uploads. Ignored discard hints preserve prior bytes and processed clip metadata; effective DISCARD invalidates VB clip records without clearing the full CPU shadow. Discarded contents remain undefined under the D3D contract. Actual production C runs 1344 cases per API with exact uploads and failure/range checks; 16 MiB guard mappings detect unwanted full-shadow clearing. Real XP validates 2688 matrix cases, 28 COM checks of the seven XP HRESULT combinations and eight known-color draw frames. Wire verifies all baseline/write bytes, 168 read-only skips, normalized hints and scene update order; no refresh hides the direct read-only-conflict uploads. SwiftShader/Metal pass 24 color probes each. A wire-valid post-capture red-to-blue corruption is rejected only by the pixel comparison, with zero host/GPU errors. D3D8/9 shipping bytes are the accepted final XP probes; DDraw shipping binaries stay at accepted 4G3 bytes. Host source/bundle and previous 44-run/533-case baseline plus 4G3 window replay are unchanged; full declared target now has 46 runs. This does not claim original Microsoft buffer-content/pixel measurements or complete buffer API validation. Remaining retail draw/copy semantics, guest wrappers, programmable CPU processing and stages 5/6 continue.
